source_documents.title: Beyond Thioflavin-T: Excited State Intramolecular Proton Transfer-Active 2-Phenylbenzimidazoles for Sensitive and Selective Detection of Insulin Amyloid Aggregates via a Unique Binding Mechanism

reference_evidence_units.quote: In a nonpolar, aprotic solvent such as toluene, (1), (2), and (3) exhibited a predominant broad emission peak in the range of 450−500 nm, corresponding to the keto tautomeric form, along with a minor peak around 370 nm, indicating negligible contribution from their enol
reference_evidence_units.statement: Keto emission at 450-500 nm dominates, with a minor enol band near 370 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state only; no ultrafast measurement (the paper says so).

reference_evidence_units.quote: These emissions features, arising from keto tautomeric forms, confirm the occurrence of ESIPT behavior in toluene with minimal enol contribution (Table S3, Supporting Information).
reference_evidence_units.statement: The keto band is read as ESIPT emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Analysis of the potential energy profiles reveals critical insight: a significant barrier for proton transfer exists in the ground state (8−10 kcal/mol)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Proton transfer is uphill in S0 and favourable in S1 (enol to keto).

reference_evidence_units.quote: In aqueous buffer, the ESIPT emission is weak due to competitive solvent quenching and nonradiative decay.

In contrast, the longer component (τ2) arises when the probes are tightly bound to the rigid, hydrophobic pockets of the amyloid fibrils, where restricted molecular motion suppresses nonradiative decay, leading to enhanced fluorescence emission and extended lifetime.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-3 bound to insulin amyloid fibrils
reference_evidence_units.statement: Turn-on in the fibril pocket is attributed to restricted motion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Needs the fibril, which is not part of the input.
